guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: Leslie West is iconically associated with a Gibson Les Paul Junior (and Jr.-style guitars), a hallmark of his thick guitar tone in Mountain.
guitar.notes: Well-documented — should not have been unknown.

tone.target: thick gritty fuzzed blues-rock crunch with upper-mid bite
tone.profile: thick gritty fuzzed blues-rock crunch with upper-mid bite
tone.summary: Fuzz -> Boost/OD -> UK 45 Amp -> UK Vintage 4x12 Cab -> EQ/Chorus for bite.

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and noise from high-gain fuzz.
Provide the thick, gritty fuzz edge required for blues-rock.
Add upper-mid bite and sustain without modern high gain.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is a general choice for classic British tone, compensating for the lack of specific Plexi/Marshall model. Using it after fuzz helps shape the core riff sound.

alternatives.reason: Could also work but might be too clean.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Marshall/Plexi sound and raw 70s feel.
Provide the classic British cabinet sound and necessary punch.
Boost the upper-mids and overall bite to cut through the mix.
Add subtle movement and width without heavy modulation.
blocks.gap: Chorus is generally avoided, but a very subtle setting can add dimension to the thick fuzz tone.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle rhythmic depth and sustain to the riffs.
blocks.gap: Used sparingly to enhance the 'thick riff sustain' without sounding overly processed.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and punch by swapping the current IR for a more aggressive, vintage British speaker simulation.

proposals.reason: Enhance the raw, aggressive punch and vintage British character needed for 'Mississippi Queen'.
